description: Probe queries used to inspect retrieval quality. Each in_corpus entry captures the initial retrieval observation, the end-to-end synthesis finding (after the LLM synthesised over retrieved chunks), and a failure_mode tag pointing at the technique that would fix the remaining real gap. The out_of_corpus entries probe whether the citation-aware prompt successfully refuses to answer when grounding is absent.

in_corpus.notes: Single-entity definitional query. Top 3 all from the Gandalf article. Baseline retrieval handles this cleanly.
in_corpus.synthesis_finding: Still good end-to-end. Top-4 all from Gandalf article. Answer cites [1][2][3] correctly, covers Istari/Olórin/Mithrandir/appearance/major deeds without leaking outside knowledge.
in_corpus.retriever_finding: hybrid-unchanged. All four retrievers H@1 (4x Gandalf). Note: BM25 only worked after fixing its default tokenizer (text.split() left 'Gandalf?' != 'Gandalf' and let stopwords dominate); pre-fix, sparse returned Figwit/Radagast for this query. A rare named entity that both dense and a properly-preprocessed BM25 nail.
in_corpus.ground_truth: Gandalf is one of the Istari (Wizards), a Maia sent by the Valar to oppose Sauron. He was known as Gandalf the Grey and later returned as Gandalf the White. The Elves called him Mithrandir. He guided the Free Peoples through the War of the Ring and was reckoned the wisest of the Maiar.

in_corpus.notes: Initial verdict 'partial / recall-not-ranking'. Bard's own article never made the candidate set; retrieval pulled Smaug-centric chunks.
in_corpus.synthesis_finding: Falsified the initial prognosis. Retrieval still pulls Smaug-centric chunks (Dragons in ME, Thorin II, Smaug, ME peoples — no Bard article), but every one of them mentions Bard, and Claude synthesised a complete answer (Bard / Black Arrow / Lake-town / thrush / Bilbo's discovery) with correct inline citations. HyDE / query decomposition is now a NICE-TO-HAVE, not the load-bearing fix. Reclassify: synthesis recovered the multi-hop.
in_corpus.retriever_finding: hybrid-regressed. Dense gets H@k (Smaug at rank 3). hybrid_50_50 keeps H@k; hybrid_40_60 and pure sparse LOSE it - BM25 over-weights Thorin/Fíli-Kíli chunks that share tokens but aren't the expected titles. Bard's own article is absent under every retriever (corpus lacks it), so this stays a synthesis case, not a retrieval win. Hybrid made it worse, not better.
in_corpus.ground_truth: Smaug was killed by Bard the Bowman, a descendant of Girion of Dale, during the dragon's attack on Lake-town. Bard shot Smaug with the Black Arrow, striking the bare patch on the dragon's underside that Bilbo had earlier discovered. Smaug fell and was destroyed.

in_corpus.query: What rings did the Dwarves get?
in_corpus.notes: Both sources' Dwarves articles surfaced. Cross-source consensus on factual queries is a positive signal.
in_corpus.synthesis_finding: Still good. Both sources' Dwarves articles + WP Dwarves-in-Middle-earth surfaced. Answer correctly distinguishes the Dwarven outcome (greed, not wraithdom) from the Men/Nazgûl outcome and traces Durin III -> Thrór -> Thráin II line. Cross-source consensus held.
in_corpus.retriever_finding: hybrid-regressed. Dense H@1 (Dwarves articles). hybrid_50_50 holds H@1; hybrid_40_60 and pure sparse MISS entirely - BM25 surfaces Ori/Thorin Oakenshield/Farmer Maggot (token co-occurrence noise) instead of the Dwarves/Rings-of-Power articles. The heavier sparse weighting hurts a query dense already nailed.
in_corpus.ground_truth: The Dwarves were given Seven Rings of Power by Sauron. Unlike the Men who received the Nine and became the Nazgûl, the Dwarves were not corrupted into wraiths; the Rings instead increased their greed for gold. Over time Sauron recovered some of the Seven and dragons consumed others.

in_corpus.query: Tell me about the Battle of Five Armies
in_corpus.notes: Initial verdict 'good-with-noise / chunk-cleaning'. The retrieved chunk leads with Fandom maintenance template text ('The descriptive majority of this article's text is unsourced...').
in_corpus.synthesis_finding: Template noise was invisible in the final answer — Claude ignored the maintenance text and gave a clean account of the battle (allies, Bolg/Gundabad, Thorin/Fíli/Kíli wounded, Beorn slays Bolg, Bilbo knocked out). Chunk cleanup is genuinely lower priority than the initial pass implied. Keep it as nice-to-have, not blocking.
in_corpus.retriever_finding: hybrid-unchanged (mild improvement). All retrievers except pure-sparse get H@1. hybrid packs two 'Battle of Five Armies' chunks into the top-4 (dense had one diluted by a Bilbo and a Gandalf chunk). No regression; marginally tighter on-topic. The one probe where hybrid is arguably a touch better.
in_corpus.ground_truth: The Battle of Five Armies was fought at the Lonely Mountain (Erebor) after Smaug's death. The five armies were Dwarves, Elves, and Men against Goblins and Wargs, with the goblin host led by Bolg. Thorin Oakenshield and his nephews Fíli and Kíli were killed, and the Eagles and Beorn turned the tide for the victory of the Free Peoples.

in_corpus.notes: Initial verdict 'partial / reranking'. Edith Tolkien's gravestone chunk surfaced at #3 and looked like wrong-context noise that a cross-encoder would demote.
in_corpus.synthesis_finding: Falsified the 'reranking is the fix' diagnosis. Claude integrated the Edith Tolkien grave chunk as a closing paragraph ('Tolkien identified himself and his wife Edith with these characters, having BEREN inscribed on his own grave marker and LUTHIEN on hers'). The chunk wasn't wrong-context — it was real biographical context the LLM used appropriately. Demoting it with a reranker would have made the answer worse, not better.
in_corpus.retriever_finding: hybrid-unchanged. Dense and both hybrids get H@1 via Lúthien (the corpus has a 'Lúthien' article but no standalone 'Beren' one, so 'Beren'/'Of Beren and Lúthien' never appear). hybrid injects Curufin/Ufedhin noise but Lúthien still leads. The initially hoped-for both-entities coverage isn't achievable here - it's a corpus-coverage limit, not a retrieval-tuning one.
in_corpus.ground_truth: Beren, a mortal Man, and Lúthien, the half-Maia daughter of the Elven King Thingol, fell in love. Thingol set a bride-price of a Silmaril from Morgoth's crown. They recovered a Silmaril together, but Beren died; for her love Lúthien chose to become mortal and they were granted a second life, dwelling on Tol Galen and having a son, Dior. (Corpus note: coverage comes from the Lúthien article; there is no standalone Beren article.)

in_corpus.notes: All three results from Wikipedia's Mithril article. Definitional 'what is X?' queries naturally favor Wikipedia's encyclopedic prose over Fandom's narrative style.
in_corpus.synthesis_finding: Still good and still Wikipedia-dominated (4/4 chunks from WP Mithril). Initial source-style observation confirmed: encyclopedic prose wins definitional queries. Etymology (mith + ril) and Hobbit/FotR quotes both made it into the answer.
in_corpus.retriever_finding: hybrid-unchanged. All four retrievers return 4x 'Mithril', H@1. The clean control: a rare, distinctive single-token entity that both dense and (fixed) sparse nail identically. No difference, no regression.
in_corpus.ground_truth: Mithril is a fictional silver-like metal in Tolkien's Middle-earth, stronger and lighter than steel. It was found and mined by the Dwarves in Moria (Khazad-dûm). It was extremely valuable; Bilbo's mithril mail shirt, later worn by Frodo, is a notable example of its use.

in_corpus.notes: Initial verdict 'partial / hybrid-search'. Bombadil's own dedicated article was not the top hit.
in_corpus.synthesis_finding: The one case the LLM CANNOT compensate for, and the most diagnostically useful query in the set. Retrieval still surfaces Middle-earth peoples / Adventures of Tom Bombadil / Barrow-wight — Bombadil's own page never enters the candidate set. Answer is good because the candidate chunks happen to summarise him, but Goldberry / Withywindle / Old Forest specifics are absent. This is the clean example of the candidate-set-miss class of failure: hybrid BM25 + dense retrieval is the load-bearing fix. Reranking won't help; synthesis can't compensate. Re-run this exact query after the retriever comparison to confirm hybrid lifts the right document into top-k.
in_corpus.retriever_finding: HYPOTHESIS FALSIFIED. still-candidate-set-miss under ALL retrievers (dense, sparse, hybrid_50_50, hybrid_40_60). Even pure BM25 - which should trivially match the literal token 'Bombadil' - never surfaces a 'Tom Bombadil' article, because the corpus does not contain one (closest is 'The Adventures of Tom Bombadil', a poetry collection). The initial diagnosis ('dense-vs-sparse, hybrid is the load-bearing fix') was WRONG: this was never a retrieval-strategy problem, it is a corpus-coverage gap. Exactly the 'watch for' the plan flagged - the failure is corpus structure, not dense vs sparse. The real fix is ingesting Bombadil's article (re-scrape / expand corpus), not any retriever change.
in_corpus.corpus_fix_finding: Corpus gap closed (fetched the Wikipedia 'Tom Bombadil' article, 30 chunks added; Chroma 5763->5793). Fair retest of the original hybrid hypothesis: dense=[Bombadil x4], sparse=[Bombadil, Middle-earth peoples, Bombadil, Bombadil], hybrid_50_50/40_60=[Bombadil, Bombadil, Bombadil, Middle-earth peoples]. ALL retrievers now H@1. The hybrid hypothesis falsified a SECOND time: dense alone is cleanest (4/4); adding BM25 slightly DILUTES (drags one generic 'Middle-earth peoples' chunk into top-4). The 'rare named entity gets dominated, BM25 rescues it' theory was wrong on both counts - dense handled the rare entity fine once the page existed, and hybrid didn't help. Dense remains the default.
in_corpus.ground_truth: Tom Bombadil is an enigmatic character in The Lord of the Rings who lives in the Old Forest with his wife Goldberry. He is unaffected by the One Ring: it does not turn him invisible and has no power over him. Tolkien deliberately left his true nature and origin unexplained.

out_of_corpus.expected_behavior: Refuse: 'context does not contain information about ...'
out_of_corpus.notes: Verifies the system prompt's 'answer only from context' constraint holds for a question that sounds Tolkien-flavoured but has no in-corpus answer.

out_of_corpus.query: What did Frodo have for breakfast on the third Tuesday of Halimath?
out_of_corpus.expected_behavior: Refuse: specific fabricated detail with no source.
out_of_corpus.notes: Probes whether Claude confabulates plausible-sounding specifics when the corpus is silent. Halimath is a real Shire-reckoning month so the question reads grounded but is unanswerable.

out_of_corpus.query: How does the One Ring compare to the rings in Wagner's Der Ring des Nibelungen?
out_of_corpus.expected_behavior: Refuse or use Outside context: prefix. Tolkien wikis discuss the One Ring extensively but not the Wagner comparison.
out_of_corpus.notes: Tests the gap between in-corpus topic (One Ring) and out-of-corpus claim (Wagner comparison). Easiest failure mode for an LLM: half the question has rich grounding, half doesn't.
